primary.summary: Category slugs are no longer made unique, so seeded categories get bare slugs like 'tools' and 'industrial' without the random suffix and can duplicate instead of 'tools-Q-mXebnHPt'.
primary.rootCause: In server/models/category.js the slug field has `unique: false`, while brand.js and product.js (the other schemas using the same mongoose-slug-generator plugin) have `unique: true`. The mongoose-slug-generator plugin only enforces slug uniqueness (appending a random suffix such as '-Q-mXebnHPt' when a colliding slug already exists) when the slug options mark the field unique. With unique: false the plugin leaves the slugified name unchanged, so the two seeded categories that resolve to the same name slug get identical slugs ('tools', 'industrial'), which shows up in every GET /api/category/list response as missing suffixes and duplicate slug values compared with the reference run.

Reference run of the same tests returned category slugs 'tools-Q-mXebnHPt' and 'industrial-hzkNnzSpCt' with no duplicates; this run returns 'tools' and 'industrial' with duplicate slug values, matching the plugin's documented non-unique behaviour.
Health checks, seed requests and seed check all passed with no incidents, so the change is data-shaping logic, not infrastructure: the DB was seeded the same way but produced different slugs.

The mongoose-slug-generator plugin only performs its uniqueness pass (checking existing documents and appending a random suffix to a colliding slug) when the slug path option unique is true, as it is in server/models/brand.js:22 and server/models/product.js:25. When categories are seeded (server/utils/seed.js:53-59 uses faker.commerce.department() which repeats department names such as 'Tools' and 'Industrial'), colliding categories are saved with a bare slug 'tools'/'industrial' instead of the uniquified 'tools-_SkpyylByB'/'industrial-RndXCEZxQD' seen in the reference, producing duplicate slugs in the list that all four tests then read back from GET /api/category.

evidence.detail: server/models/category.js:23-27 slug path has unique:false; brand.js:19-23 and product.js:22-26 use unique:true, so only category slugs are left un-uniquified by the slug plugin.

server/utils/seed.js:53-59 seeds 10 categories with faker.commerce.department() names and faker sentences descriptions ('Adipiscor claro voluptate copiose.' in the diffs); repeated names cause slug collisions.

GET /api/category in this run returns slug 'tools' and 'industrial' (plain, duplicated) where the reference returned 'tools-_SkpyylByB' and 'industrial-RndXCEZxQD'; TC-059 shows this already at its first list call, before it creates anything, so the difference is in stored seed data, not in these tests.
All four tests pass; the differences only appear in the recorded GET /api/category responses, i.e. the tests do not assert slug uniqueness, but the data is wrong.

suggestedFix.description: Set unique: true on the Category slug path (like Brand and Product) so the slug-generator plugin appends a uniqueness suffix when seeded names collide; also re-seed/re-restore the database so existing duplicate category slugs are regenera.

primary.summary: The email validation in POST /api/contact/add is inverted (`if (email)`), so an empty body falls through to the name check and a submission with an email is wrongly rejected.
primary.rootCause: In server/routes/api/contact.js the guard at line 14 reads `if (email)` instead of `if (!email)`. With an empty body, email is undefined so the check is skipped and the handler reaches the `!name` check, returning 'You must enter description & name.' instead of 'You must enter an email address.' (E2 fails). Conversely any valid submission containing an email is rejected with status 400, which is why later calls (2, 3, 4) in the reference run show 400/200 while this run got no such calls' expected responses — every request with an email errors out.

TC-089 E2 expected 'You must enter an email address.' for empty body but received 'You must enter description & name.'
REQ-049 expects missing email to yield 'You must enter an email address.' and otherwise-valid submissions to succeed.

suggestedFix.description: Change line 14 to `if (!email)` so the email-missing error is returned when the email field is absent, and submissions containing an email are validated normally.
